summary: Cunda studied under Ajahn Pasanno and Ajahn Amaro.

Cuong T. Mai is a scholar in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He earned an MA from the University of Hawaiʻi and a PhD from Indiana University under John R. McRae, later serving as an adjunct lecturer at the University of Vermont.

Cynthea J. Bogel specializes in Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under doctoral supervisor John M. Rosenfield and Keizaburo Mizuno, and held a post at the University of Washington (attested 2004–2009).
Cynthia Col works in Sinology and religious studies. She studied Chinese religion at the Graduate Theological Union (attested 2003) and was taught by Mark Elliott and Steven D. Goodman.
Cynthia M. Beall is a Tibetologist who studied at Pennsylvania State University from circa 1971 to 1976. She joined Case Western Reserve University in 1976.

Cynthia Talbot is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at the University of Wisconsin–Madison from circa 1980 to 1988 and took up a post at the University of Texas at Austin circa 1994.

Cyril Henry Philips was a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Liverpool and SOAS University of London. He served as Director of SOAS from 1957, succeeding Ralph Lilley Turner, and as Vice-Chancellor of the University of London (1972–1976).

Cyrus Stearns specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA under Turrell V. Wylie and a PhD from the University of Washington under Leonard van der Kuijp, studied under several Tibetan masters, and served as a translator for the Tsadra Foundation.
Cécile Ducher works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD under Matthew T. Kapstein at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, where she also held a position as a research fellow.

D. C. Lau was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. After studying at the University of Hong Kong and the University of Glasgow, he taught at SOAS, University College London, the University of London, and The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
D. C. Sarasvati is an Indologist who studied under V. Raghavan and served as Lecturer-cum-Research Assistant at the University of Madras from 1964 to 1965.

D. Dennis Hudson was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He spent his career at Smith College, teaching in the Department of Religion and serving as Professor in the Department of Religion and Biblical Studies from circa 1970 to 2004.
D. L. Narasimhachar was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore, from circa 1925 to 1929, and held a post at the University of Mysore from circa 1932 to 1962.

D. Neil Schmid is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the University of Pennsylvania, where he was a doctoral student under Victor H. Mair.
D. R. Nagaraj was an Indologist who studied at Bangalore University from circa 1975 to 1980 and subsequently held an academic post there from circa 1980 to 1998.

D. R. Shackleton Bailey was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and classics. Educated at Cambridge, he held fellowships and posts at Gonville and Caius College, Jesus College, Cambridge, the University of Michigan, and served as Pope Professor of Latin at Harvard.
D. S. Subbaramaiya was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under traditional teachers Mallikere Subrahmanya Sastri and V. S. Ramachandra Sastri.

D. Srinivasachar was an Indologist attested between 1931 and 1933 as Professor of Sanskrit at Maharaja's College, Mysore, and Curator at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore, succeeding Rudrapatna Shamasastry.

Dagfinn Føllesdal was a philosopher and linguist. Educated at the University of Oslo and Harvard under W. V. O. Quine, he taught at Harvard, the University of Oslo, and Stanford University, where he was Clarence Irving Lewis Professor of Philosophy Emeritus.
Dagmar Schwerk is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Hamburg from circa 2010 to 2017, completing her doctorate under Dorji Wangchuk.
